english.title: Person with a debt relief order obtain credit / engage in business without disclosing status / name
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person in respect of whom a debt relief order had been made, during the relevant period as defined in section 251S(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986,

(A)_[obtained credit without giving **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), the person from whom you obtained the credit, the relevant information about your status]_
(B)_[engaged in a business under the name of **(..SPECIFY NAME..) which was a name other than that in which the order had been made without disclosing to all persons with whom you entered into a business transaction the name in which the order had been made]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 251S(1), 251T(3) and 430 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.

english.notes:
(i) For the purposes of this section, the relevant information about a person's status is the information that
(a) a moratorium is in force in relation to the debt relief order
(b) a debt relief restrictions order is in force in respect of him; or
(c) both a moratorium and a debt relief restrictions order is in force
as the case may be.
(ii) 'Relevant period' means -
(a) the moratorium period relating to the debt relief order, or
(b) the period for which a debt relief restrictions order is in force in respect of the person in respect of whom the debt relief order is made
(iii) Subsection (1)(a) does not apply if the amount of credit is less than the prescribed amount (if any) - section 251S(4)
(iv) The reference in subsection (1)(a) to a person obtaining credit includes the following cases -
(a) where the goods are bailed to him under a hire-purchase agreement, or agreed to be sold to him under a conditional sale agreement;
(b) where he is paid in advance (money or otherwise) for the supply of good services
(v) This offence was Inserted by section 108(1) of and Schedule 17 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years and / or a fine.

Note: In relation to offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (limit on magistrates' court powers to impose imprisonment), the reference to "twelve months" is to be read as a reference to "six months".

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
